old_title: Ukraine war live: Kyiv's Starlink access remains limited despite Trump's claims
new_title: Ukraine war live: Explosions rock Russian petrochemical plant hit by drones

US president Donald Trump claims SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has restored Ukraine's Starlink access, even as Volodymyr Zelensky and Ukrainian sources said there had been no change in satellite internet speeds.
Trump refused to confirm reports that he had called Musk to ask him to restore the service for Ukraine's military, saying: "I don't want to comment on it, whether I called or whether somebody else called ... The bottom line - he put it back."
Meanwhile, the Ukrainian president warned that his Russian counterpart, Vladimir Putin, now believes his maximalist war goals - which include capturing four Ukrainian regions in their entirety - are within reach.
"Russia is clearly taking advantage of the slowdown in air defence supplies from our partners," Zelensky wrote in a post on X on Thursday.
"It is equally clear that when some partners ease the pressure on Russia, it only reinforces Putin's belief that his goals are within reach. We need different signals and different steps - stronger ones."
Speaking a day after meeting Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff, Putin insisted that Russia was not preparing for war with Europe and that trilateral talks should be about ensuring the future security of both countries.
A Ukrainian soldier blinded in war hopes to see his children again, in photos
Ukrainian soldier Mykola Kasiuk hopes to regain some vision after a battlefield land mine explosion left him nearly blind two years ago. After numerous operations, he is turning to visiting US surgeons in Kyiv, hoping to see his children again.
Sister of American held in Russia says he didn't know he was being released until he saw US flag
The younger sister of Stephen Hubbard, the US citizen freed Wednesday after spending more than four years in a Russian prison, said her brother didn't realise he was being released until he was put aboard a plane and saw the American flag.
"He didn't know why he was being taken from the prison to Moscow, and he may have thought he was going to his death," Patricia Hubbard Fox said during an interview Thursday in San Antonio, where her brother was taken for evaluation.
"He's been kind of laughing a lot," she added. "Like relief laughing. 'Oh my God, you know, I'm free. This is really happening.'"
President Donald Trump said he had asked Russian President Vladimir Putin during a phone call earlier this month to free Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired teacher from Michigan.
Hubbard was accused of fighting alongside Kyiv's forces after Russia's full-scale invasion of the country in 2022.
Kremlin continues to demand Ukraine cede more land
After meeting Volodymyr Zelensky and European and Nato officials in Oslo this week, Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff spoke of "some degree of momentum", but the Kremlin expressed doubts.
"The Americans sensed some new nuances (in Oslo) and told us about this. But these nuances, so to speak, do not entirely satisfy us," Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said on Thursday.
A senior Russian official, briefed on the Putin-Witkoff talks, said they were relatively short and not substantive. The American brought proposals drafted in Oslo and handed them to Putin for review, the person said.
Another source close to the Kremlin said the US proposals included a scenario where Ukraine would cede its Donbas region to Russia in return for receiving a guarantee of its future security from Nato.
Moscow has repeatedly said it would not end fighting unless Ukraine cedes more land, limits the size of its forces and is permanently barred from forming alliances.
Ukraine dismisses Russia's conditions as a demand for capitulation that would leave it defenceless.
Russian strikes cut power to over 500,000 in Ukraine
Russia attacked energy facilities in six Ukrainian regions overnight on Friday, knocking out power for more than 500,000 people, Deputy Energy Minister Artem Nekrasov said.
Austria expels four Russian diplomats on security grounds
Austria's foreign ministry said on Friday it was expelling four Vienna-based Russian diplomats over "activities incompatible with their diplomatic status", a term usually used for spying.
"Based on findings by the Austrian security authorities, the Austrian foreign ministry has taken measures against four Russian diplomats in Vienna," it said in a statement, adding that they had been declared personae non gratae and ordered to leave the country.
Three of them worked at Russia's embassy to Austria and one at the Russian delegation to the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) on military security and arms control, the ministry said.
The move brings to 18 the number of Russian diplomats Austria has expelled since 2020. While Austria is a neutral country, politically its governments have sided with Ukraine since Russia launched its all-out invasion in 2022. The Russian embassy did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Russia will respond to Austria's decision, Russian news agencies cited a foreign ministry official as saying on Friday.
Ukrainian energy company says Russian attack hit one of its power stations
Ukraine's largest private energy company, DTEK, said on Friday a Russian attack has hit one of its thermal power plants, which has halted operations due to significant damage. It did not say where the plant is located.
Russian tanker heads for New York with 40,000 tons of diesel after Trump-Putin deal
A Malta-flagged tanker transporting 40,000 metric tons of Russian diesel is en route to New York following a deal reached with US President Donald Trump, LSEG shipping data showed on Friday.
Trump has taken several measures to lower domestic fuel prices ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, including waiving parts of a recent Russian sanctions law and threatening Europe with a US diesel export ban unless countries release emergency reserves.
Russia bombs Kyiv despite renewing negotiations
Russia pounded Kyiv with ballistic missiles and Ukraine sent hundreds of drones towards Moscow on Thursday, as the warring sides kept up a barrage of attacks despite the latest US push to end the conflict.
Ukraine said Russia fired at least 21 ballistic missiles in three waves. President Volodymyr Zelensky said three carried cluster munitions - "bomblets" that disperse over a wide area and are banned by many countries because of the danger to civilians.
Russia's defence ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.Russia said Ukraine launched 630 drones towards Moscow during the night.
Ukraine seeks to move customs checks inside EU to avoid Russian drones - report
Ukraine is in talks with EU member states Poland and Slovakia about moving customs checks on lorries carrying grain exports from the border to inside those countries, to halt Russian drone attacks on the trucks, the Financial Times reported.
Ukraine's foreign ministry said Kyiv had set up joint border control points with Moldova and wanted to "scale up" the initiative with other neighbours, including Poland, the FT reported.
Ministry spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi told the paper the move was driven by a "new security environment where Russia is deliberately trying to strike our borders" and that Kyiv wanted to finalise an agreement with Poland as soon as possible.
Russia hits Ukraine's port of Vilkovo
The Russian military has hit the port of Vilkovo in the Odesa region in Ukraine, a railcar depot in the Poltava region and a cargo vessel in the Black Sea, the Russian defence ministry said on Telegram.
It added that all were used for military purposes.

Ukrainian forces struck a Russian petrochemical plant in Togliatti overnight, Kyiv's general staff said on Saturday.
Footage circulating on social media showed thick black smoke rising from the industrial area.
The attack caused an explosion and fire, Ukrainian authorities said on Telegram. Togloatti mayor Ilya Sukhikh said several industrial facilities were damaged in the attack.
The city in western Russia is home to the country's largest carmaker Avtovaz and major ammonia producer Togliattiazot.
It comes as the White House praised Melania Trump for reportedly securing a ceasefire for the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, where up to 2,000 residents are cut off from world and facing starvation.
Russia agreed to pause all military action in Oleshky to allow for humanitarian aid to enter and to prepare a civilian evacuation through a designated safe passageway, according to the White House.
The localised ceasefire will begin on October 29.
A post on the White House's social media account on Friday said: "Our incredible @FLOTUS Melania Trump has forged a ceasefire in war-torn Oleshky. Peace through strength."
Explosions rock Russian petrochemical plant hit by drone strike
Ukrainian forces struck a Russian petrochemical plant in Togliatti overnight, Kyiv's general staff said on Saturday.
The attack caused an explosion and fire, it said on the Telegram app.
Togliatti is home to Russia's largest carmaker Avtovaz and major ammonia producer Togliattiazot.
Togloatti mayor Ilya Sukhikh said several industrial facilities were damaged in the attack.
Three Russian diesel tankers head to North America under US deal
Three tankers carrying Russian diesel are heading towards North America, Russian deputy prime minister Alexander Novak said on Friday.
The shipments are part of a deal that could see Russia supply 500,000 metric tonnes of fuel to US and global markets in October, he said.
"The first three fuel tankers are already on their way to the eastern coast of the Atlantic Ocean, with significant support from the RDIF (Russian Direct Investment Fund)," Novak said.
Under a deal announced by US president Donald Trump this month, Washington temporarily lifted sanctions on Russian fuel in exchange for supplies aimed at lowering global fuel prices.
Reuters reported that one tanker, the Malta-flagged Agioi Fanendes, carrying ultra-low sulphur diesel, is expected to arrive in the US on 7 November.
US lawmakers demand answers from Musk over Ukraine Starlink restrictions
Six Democratic US lawmakers have demanded that Elon Musk explain restrictions on Starlink and its military version, Starshield, which have disrupted Ukrainian military operations.
They gave Musk until 31 October to answer five questions, warning that his control over another country's military communications raised concerns about corporate governance and geopolitical risks.
"As a publicly traded company, SpaceX has a legal obligation to disclose to shareholders and the public material events that could affect your business model," the lawmakers wrote in the letter.
"The revelation that you personally wielded control over a foreign country's military communications would require disclosure of elevated risks for corporate governance, geopolitical exposure, and potential adverse actions by foreign governments."
Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the disruptions were ongoing, saying: "The speed restrictions for Starlink and Starshield are still in effect. The speed has not been restored. And the supply of interceptor missiles to protect against Russian ballistic missiles is still delayed."
Mass blackouts reported across occupied Crimea
A key electrical substation in southern Russia was reportedly damaged in an overnight attack on Saturday, triggering widespread power outages across Moscow-occupied Crimea, according to Telegram monitoring channels.
"The entire peninsula is without electricity," the Telegram channel Exilenova+ reported on the evening of 23 October, The Kyiv Independent reported.
Satellite imagery from NASA FIRMS reportedly indicated that an overnight attack damaged the Taman substation in Russia's Krasnodar Krai, which supplies electricity to occupied Crimea.
Major cities, including Sevastopol and Yalta, were left without power.
"As a result of an enemy attack on energy infrastructure outside of Sevastopol, our city is temporarily without power," Sevastopol's Russian-installed governor Mykhailo Razvozhaev said on Telegram.
Internet monitoring group NetBlocks also reported widespread internet outages across Crimea.
Ukraine has not commented on the attack yet.
Zelensky criticises Trump administration's actions as 'not supportive'
Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky has expressed frustration with the Trump administration's recent actions towards Kyiv, describing them as "not supportive".
In an interview with ABC News, Zelensky appeared to take a swipe at US special envoy Steve Witkoff, who recently praised Russian president Vladimir Putin as "a humanitarian".
Zelensky said: "I'm a normal person. I'm just human. Maybe not such a big humanitarian as Putin, of course."
He focused on Ukraine's urgent military needs, saying Starlink was still not operating at full speed on the battlefield, despite Donald Trump's claims to the contrary.
Saving children is the US first lady's focus, Trump says, as Melania secures ceasefire for Ukrainian town
Melania Trump has made helping children in conflict zones one of her signature issues in her husband's second term.
She hosted a UN Security Council meeting on the issue earlier this year, and last year wrote to Russian president Vladimir Putin about efforts to reunite families with children who have been displaced by the war.
She has helped reunite nearly three dozen children, according to her senior adviser, Marc Beckman.
"What she wants to do is save children, and that's her focus," the president told reporters at the White House.
Ukraine and Russia swap prisoners in 'very important result'
Ukraine and Russia swapped 270 servicemen each in a prisoner exchange yesterday, the Russian defence ministry said.
Ukrainian president described the swap, the first since August, as a "very important result".
Ukraine's acting prosecutor, Anton Kovalskyi, writing on Telegram, said more than 19,000 Ukrainian civilians, including 762 children, had been killed since Russia launched its full-scale war more than four years ago.
A drone hit and sank a cargo vessel in new Black Sea attack near Romania, killing 1
A drone hit and sank a cargo vessel in the Black Sea on Friday, killing one crew member and leaving three missing, officials said, in the latest attack on commercial shipping in the region that has raised fears of an escalation in Russia's war against Ukraine.
Romanian naval authorities said that a search and rescue mission was underway after the ship caught fire and sank about 13 nautical miles (15 miles) east of the port city of Constanta, near Romania's territorial waters. The crew consisted of 10 Ukrainian citizens and three Azerbaijanis. Nine were rescued.
Melania Trump claims to have secured ceasefire for single Ukrainian town in surprising peace breakthrough
Melania Trump says she has secured a ceasefire for a Ukrainian city that was until now cut off from the world and facing starvation.
The Russian-occupied city of Oleshky is located at the frontline and is made up of 2,000 residents who have faced an ongoing blockade restricting food and aid.
But the First Lady said on Friday that Russia has agreed to pause all military action in the town to allow for humanitarian aid to enter and to prepare a civilian evacuation through a designated safe passageway, according to the White House.
